links.outcome: Harmful LLM behavior following user risky belief or behavior expressions across multi-turn conversations
links.effect: Harmful behavior followed 74% of risky belief expressions and 73% of risky behavior expressions, versus 28% of turns without preceding risk expressions; harmful responses often persisted across turns.
links.quote: Harmful behavior followed 74% of risky belief expressions and 73% of risky behavior expressions, versus 28% of turns without preceding risk expressions.

unlisted_practices: Multi-turn clinician-informed behavioral annotation of epistemic quality (helpful vs harmful labels based on Self-Determination Theory) for LLMs
Evaluating LLM correction latency and recovery from harmful behavior across conversation turns

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation/benchmark framework (mPACT-MIS-v1.0) assessing epistemic drift, risky beliefs, and model behaviors across simulated multi-turn conversations in LLMs, but does not test a specific deployment practice or safeguard.
